outline.chapter_title: Mathematical Reasoning with LLMs: Motivation, Challenges, and DeepSeekMath at a Glance
outline.description: Introduce why mathematical reasoning is difficult for language models, the open vs. closed model landscape, and how DeepSeekMath advances the state of the art through data, pretraining, instruction tuning, and reinforcement learning.
subtopics: Why mathematical reasoning is hard: symbolic structure, multi-step logic, precision
Benchmark-driven progress and the gap between open and closed models
DeepSeekMath goals and key contributions
High-level pipeline: corpus construction → base pretraining → instruction tuning → RL
Headline results: 51.7% on MATH without tools, 60.9% with self-consistency (64), GSM8K 88.2%
Positioning vs. GPT-4, Gemini-Ultra, and open-source peers

outline.chapter_title: Benchmarks and Evaluation Protocols for Mathematical Reasoning
outline.description: Survey the benchmarks, task formats, and evaluation settings used to measure math reasoning, including tool-augmented and formal mathematics evaluations.
subtopics: English benchmarks: GSM8K, MATH, SAT, OCW Courses, MMLU-STEM, BBH
Chinese benchmarks: MGSM-zh, CMATH, Gaokao-MathCloze, Gaokao-MathQA
Formal mathematics: miniF2F with Isabelle and Sledgehammer
Evaluation modes: tool-free CoT, program-of-thought (PoT), tool-integrated reasoning
Decoding strategies: temperature sampling, self-consistency, Maj@K vs Pass@K
Contamination risks and strict filtering policies

outline.chapter_title: Constructing the DeepSeekMath Corpus from Common Crawl
outline.description: Detail the scalable pipeline that mines high-quality math content from public web data, emphasizing classifier design, iterative mining, multilingual coverage, and contamination control.
subtopics: Seed corpus: leveraging OpenWebMath as positive examples
fastText classifier training: features, hyperparameters, negatives
Common Crawl deduplication: URL-based and near-duplicate removal
High-score ranking and token volume selection (40B, 80B, 120B, 160B)
Domain-level mining with manual URL annotation and iteration
Final corpus: 35.5M pages, 120B tokens, multilingual composition
Decontamination via n-gram exact matching for English and Chinese benchmarks
Human-in-the-loop refinement and quality gates

outline.chapter_title: Validating Corpus Quality: Size, Multilinguality, and Comparisons
outline.description: Present controlled pretraining experiments that compare DeepSeekMath Corpus against MathPile, OpenWebMath, and Proof-Pile-2, highlighting quality, scaling, and multilingual benefits.
subtopics: Controlled setup with a 1.3B parameter model (optimizer, schedule, batch, context)
Learning curves: stronger improvements and slower saturation
Outperforming Proof-Pile-2 after fewer tokens (higher average quality)
Multilingual advantage: English and Chinese math gains
Size matters with quality: why larger curated web math helps
Key takeaway: curated web math outperforms arXiv-heavy corpora in this setting

outline.chapter_title: Pretraining DeepSeekMath-Base 7B: Data, Recipe, and Baseline Performance
outline.description: Explain the continual pretraining of a 7B model initialized from a code model, the data mixture, training recipe, and comprehensive evaluations across math, tools, formal math, and general capabilities.
subtopics: Initialization from DeepSeek-Coder-Base-v1.5 7B
Data mixture: 56% DeepSeekMath Corpus, 4% AlgebraicStack, 10% arXiv, 20% GitHub code, 10% general CC (EN/zh)
Training setup: 500B tokens, learning rate and batch choices
Tool-free reasoning: leading open-source base performance; GSM8K ~64.2%, MATH ~36.2%
Program-aided reasoning (PoT): surpassing Llemma 34B on GSM8K and MATH
Formal math: few-shot autoformalization on miniF2F with Isabelle
Generalization: boosts on MMLU and BBH; preserves coding on HumanEval and MBPP

outline.chapter_title: What Training Data Matters? Code Helps, arXiv Often Doesn’t
outline.description: Analyze ablations showing the benefits of code training for math reasoning and the limited gains from arXiv-only training, with practical insights on stage ordering and catastrophic forgetting.
subtopics: Two-stage vs one-stage training designs
Code-first then math: improves tool-free and tool-based math reasoning
Mixed code+math one-stage: mitigates catastrophic forgetting, boosts PoT
Capacity considerations at smaller scales (1.3B) for joint learning
ArXiv-only training: minimal or negative impact on targeted benchmarks
Caveats: task specificity, combinations with other data, scaling to larger models

outline.chapter_title: Mathematical Instruction Tuning: Data Curation, Formats, and Results
outline.description: Describe the 776K-example instruction corpus, training setup, and how DeepSeekMath-Instruct 7B competes with larger and closed models under tool-free and tool-augmented settings.
subtopics: Dataset composition: English (GSM8K, MATH, MathInstruct subset, Lila-OOD), Chinese K-12 across 76 subtopics
Reasoning formats: chain-of-thought, program-of-thought, tool-integrated
Training setup: 4K context, 500 steps, batch 256, learning rate 5e-5
Tool-free results: strong MATH accuracy vs open-source and many closed models
With tools: approaching 60% on MATH; competitive with much larger chat models
Gaps vs GPT-4 and Gemini-Ultra: remaining room for improvement

outline.chapter_title: Foundations of RL for LLM Reasoning: From PPO to Process Rewards
outline.description: Provide the prerequisites for understanding DeepSeekMath’s RL phase: PPO, reward shaping and KL control, outcome vs process supervision, and online vs offline data collection.
subtopics: Why RL after SFT improves reasoning robustness
PPO essentials: actor-critic, GAE, clipped ratios
KL regularization to a reference model
Challenges of value modeling in long-form generation
Outcome vs process supervision: end answers vs step-level signals
Online vs offline sampling: exploration benefits and pitfalls

outline.chapter_title: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO): Design, Theory, and Variants
outline.description: Introduce GRPO as a memory-efficient PPO variant that replaces the critic with a group-based baseline, detail its objective, and cover outcome, process, and iterative extensions.
subtopics: Motivation: remove the critic to reduce memory and instability
Group sampling: using average group reward as a baseline
GRPO objective: clipped policy ratios with KL on loss (not reward)
Unbiased KL estimator and its stability advantages
Outcome-supervision GRPO: normalized group rewards as advantages
Process-supervision GRPO: step-level rewards and cumulative advantages
Iterative GRPO: reward model replay, reference model updates
Practical hyperparameters: group size 64, policy lr 1e-6, KL coeff 0.04, max length 1024, batch 1024
Compute efficiency and training loop structure

outline.chapter_title: RL Training and Empirical Findings: GRPO vs RFT/DPO/PPO and Why RL Works
outline.description: Unify SFT, RFT, DPO, PPO, and GRPO under a single gradient paradigm; report DeepSeekMath-RL results; analyze online vs offline sampling, outcome vs process supervision, and explain robustness gains.
subtopics: Unified gradient view: data source, reward function, algorithm (gradient coefficients)
Mapping SFT, RFT, DPO, PPO, GRPO into the paradigm
RL setup: 144K CoT questions (GSM8K, MATH) only; reward model from Base 7B
Online vs offline: GRPO > Online RFT > RFT; benefits of real-time exploration
Outcome vs process supervision: process generally better
Iterative RL: reward model updates and replay improve results, especially early
Why RL works: improves Maj@K more than Pass@K (distribution robustness over raw ability)
Self-consistency: 64-sample gains and practical decoding tips

outline.description: Offer hands-on guidance for reproducing training and evaluation across stages, including decoding, tool usage, formal math pipelines, contamination control, and compute budgeting.
subtopics: Training frameworks (e.g., HAI-LLM), optimizer and schedule summaries
Decoding: temperature, nucleus, self-consistency; setting sample counts
Tool-integrated evaluation: safe Python execution and SymPy
Formal math evaluation with Isabelle and Sledgehammer
Benchmark hygiene: strict decontamination with n-gram matching
Memory and throughput trade-offs; benefits of removing the critic
Reporting standards: prompts, seeds, sampling configs

outline.description: Critically assess remaining weaknesses, data biases, and alignment challenges; outline research opportunities in data, algorithms, and reward modeling, and discuss responsible dataset use.
subtopics: Current gaps: geometry and theorem-proof vs closed models
Few-shot weakness vs GPT-4; scale and data coverage factors
Potential data selection bias in pretraining and SFT
Reward models: generalization, uncertainty calibration, process RM quality
Advanced sampling for exploration (e.g., tree search) and efficient inference
Robust RL under noisy rewards; weak-to-strong alignment
Extending the pipeline to other domains (e.g., coding) and languages
Ethical considerations in web-scale data mining and benchmark integrity
